body: Why do we need a key here since we're not in a list? Same question for previous, next and last.
Not blocking, but since we're not using `pages` anywhere else, it could be inlined so the code is visually in the same order as the visual representation.
we actually are in a list: `[first, previous, ...pages, next, last]`
sure, this was just closer to the previous implementation, I prefer it inline too
This element is not part of an array, is it? It should be stable.
This default props pattern doesn't work well with TypeScript, it lies about some fields being optional, while they can't be. We could default the props line 41 when destructuring.
It is not needed here, as @sarahdayan explained.

This is the syntax we use everywhere else. (Same applies in other places.)

```suggestion
            ariaLabel="First"
```
Why introduce a new API when we can use the native `className` prop?
We could reduce nesting by having two variables: `itemClassName` and `linkClassName`. The object as a whole doesn't hold any specific meaning.
